ba145_analysis.mechanism: Odd neutron blocks pair scattering in Delta l=3, Delta j=3 channel (2f7/2 <-> 1i13/2), pushing octupole phonon excitation above 670 keV and quenching ground-state octupole collectivity by a factor of ~10.

ra225_analysis.mechanism: Intrinsic reflection asymmetry survives single-particle blocking; opposite-parity states form nearly degenerate parity doublet bands at ground state, with hallmark opposite-sign Coriolis decoupling signatures a+ ~ -a- generating alternating signature staggering.

features.145Ba (Lanthanide N~89): Soft vibrator with shallow minimum around beta3 ~ 0, high tunneling barrier absent
features.225Ra (Actinide N~137): Deformed double-well with stable minimum at beta3 ~ 0.12, finite tunneling barrier

features.145Ba (Lanthanide N~89): Severe: odd nu 1h9/2 blocks 2f7/2-1i13/2 pair scattering, octupole phonon pushed to Ex > 670 keV, B(E3) quenched by ~10x
features.225Ra (Actinide N~137): Moderate: multiple driving pairs (nu 2g9/2-1j15/2, pi 2f7/2-1i13/2) maintain collective octupole core, doublet forms at ground state

features.145Ba (Lanthanide N~89): Standard decoupled odd-A rotational band (5/2-, 7/2-, 9/2-), no opposite-parity partners below 600 keV
features.225Ra (Actinide N~137): Interleaved parity doublet bands (1/2+, 1/2-), mean energy splitting only Delta E0 = 31.3 keV

features.145Ba (Lanthanide N~89): One-body signature splitting governed by single-parity Nilsson wave function
features.225Ra (Actinide N~137): Opposite-sign decoupling parameters a+ = -a- induce sign-alternating splitting (+55, -11, +95, -42 keV)

features.145Ba (Lanthanide N~89): Octupole phonon transitions are vibrational; low-energy ground transitions have near-zero E1
features.225Ra (Actinide N~137): Inter-band E1 transitions connect doublet partners directly (B(E1) ~ 10^-3 - 10^-4 W.u.)

synthesis: The contrast between 145Ba and 225Ra establishes a rigorous microscopic criterion: parity doublets at low spin require a static reflection-asymmetric barrier capable of surviving single-particle blocking. In contrast, in nuclei with dynamic/soft octupole correlations (145Ba), blocking quenches low-energy octupole collectivity and pushes octupole phonons to high excitation energies.
